result:
Favorites added. `swift build` succeeds and `swift test` passes all 58 tests, including 6 new ones. Nothing is committed.

- **Store:** `FavoritesStore` and `UserDefaultsFavoritesStore` are in `Services/FavoritesStore.swift`. The store takes an injectable `UserDefaults` suite and saves the encoded `Movie` values in insertion order.
- **Model changes:** `Movie` is now `Codable`. I added `Movie(detail:)` because the detail screen only has a `MovieDetail`. I also added `TMDBDate.string(from:)` so release dates survive the round trip.
- **View model:** `FavoritesViewModel` has `favorites`, `isFavorite(_:)`, `toggle(_:)` and `remove(at:)`. It drops duplicate ids when loading from the store.
- **Views:** `FavoritesView` has swipe to delete and an empty state. `MovieDetailView` shows a heart button in the toolbar once the movie has loaded.
- **Tests:** `FavoritesTests.swift` covers toggle on/off, persistence across instances, order, removal and no duplicates. It also checks the encode/decode round trip. Each test uses its own `UserDefaults` suite and removes it afterwards.

Nothing in the package creates the shared `FavoritesViewModel` or shows `FavoritesView`; there is no app root. The host app must call `.environment(FavoritesViewModel())` once, high in the view tree, and must add a way to reach `FavoritesView`. Until it does, the heart button stays hidden. `FavoritesView` needs the same environment value, and it crashes without it.
